hypothesis: SetDamageCallback callback argument 2 is a DamageData object
consequence: Treat argument 2 as a number. Calling GetHealthDamage, GetShieldDamage, or GetOverguardDamage on it caused repeated live runtime errors.

hypothesis: The scalar passed to RadialDamageData:SetBaseAmount equals actual applied victim damage
consequence: SetBaseAmount is configured before victim resolution. Use the numeric SetDamageCallback result when an actual per-target result is required.

hypothesis: A Lua FindAll snapshot around the Mallet center reproduces RadialDamage victim selection
consequence: The approximation missed outer-ring ranged victims and appeared melee-only. Let Region:RadialDamage own selection.

hypothesis: A latest DamageControl record is a stable mutable object that can be retained across hits
consequence: Reacquire engine-owned state when needed; do not assume Lua wrapper identity persists across events.

hypothesis: The first SetDamageCallback callback argument is an Avatar or DamageData
consequence: Keep it typed unknown until a controlled probe or readable stock consumer establishes its contract.

hypothesis: SetOverguardAmount adds to the existing pool
consequence: It is used as an absolute setter. Read current value, compute the new absolute value, and pass only the positive delta to NotifyOverguardGain.
